properties.name: Murray Buttes Boxwork
properties.why: Eroded boxwork ridges in sulfate/mudstone layers — the primary science goal of this Marswalk.
properties.detail: Curiosity documented boxwork formations at Murray Buttes: erosion-resistant veins form ridge networks as surrounding mudstone weathers away. These record the chemistry of ancient groundwater that likely supported a habitable environment. Rapin et al. (2021) identified similar sulfate-bearing boxwork ridges as evidence of cyclical wet/dry periods.
properties.selectionNote: Our selection based on Curiosity traverse data

properties.name: Glen Torridon Clay Unit
properties.why: Strongest evidence of a long-lived ancient lake. Clay minerals form only when water persists for thousands of years.
properties.detail: Glen Torridon hosts the largest clay mineral deposits found by Curiosity. Bristow et al. (2021) showed iron-magnesium smectite clays require prolonged water contact to form — strong evidence the ancient lake in Gale Crater persisted for geologically significant time. A human geologist could sample fresh outcrop faces inaccessible to the rover arm.
properties.source: Bristow et al. (2021), Science Advances, doi:10.1126/sciadv.abh3023
properties.selectionNote: Our selection based on Curiosity traverse data

properties.name: Vera Rubin Ridge
properties.why: Hematite-rich layer formed in ancient standing water. The ridge is a natural waypoint and navigation landmark.
properties.detail: Vera Rubin Ridge is an iron-oxide (hematite) bearing unit that forms a prominent east-west ridge. Fraeman et al. (2020) showed the hematite formed in acidic to neutral standing water. Its hardness made it resistant to erosion, creating a natural path along the ridge with panoramic views of the crater floor below.
properties.source: Fraeman et al. (2020), JGR Planets, doi:10.1029/2019JE006306
properties.selectionNote: Our selection based on Curiosity traverse data

properties.name: Gediz Vallis Channel
properties.why: Possible water-carved channel on the flank of Mount Sharp. Could reveal the most recent wet period on Mars.
properties.detail: Gediz Vallis is an erosional channel cutting through the sulfate unit of Mount Sharp. NASA (2023) reported that Curiosity found evidence the channel was carved by liquid water relatively recently in Mars history, potentially billions of years after the ancient lake dried up. A human explorer could investigate channel walls and floor deposits unreachable by the rover.
properties.source: NASA/JPL press release, 2023; MSL Science Team
properties.selectionNote: Our selection based on Curiosity traverse data

properties.name: Greenheugh Pediment
properties.why: Erosion-resistant sandstone cap preserving a climate transition layer — evidence of a drier Mars era following the ancient lake.
properties.detail: Greenheugh Pediment is a broad, gently-sloping erosional surface capped by coarse sandstone. Edgar et al. (2020) showed it records a major climate transition: sandstone deposited by wind (an aeolian process) overlies older lake-deposited mudstone, marking the moment the persistent lake dried. A human explorer at this boundary could collect samples at the contact zone.
properties.source: Edgar et al. (2020), JGR Planets, doi:10.1029/2020JE006527
